activities.caption: rebuild the arc from flat start to untying
activities.name: hrArcOrder

config.prompt: The dramatic arc's five parts, in order:
items: Rising action — complications stack, each making the original question harder to answer
Climax — the question answers itself, the moment everything has been aiming at
Denouement — French for 'untying', the knot loosened
config.why: The curve is a promise of escalation: readers tolerate long quiet passages early only because the climb has begun.

activities.anchor: That last observation is the practical one
activities.caption: bet before you read on
activities.name: hrBudgetPredict

config.q: A story opens with its biggest explosion. Judged from the end, how does it usually feel?
config.why: Tension is a budget: spent early, it leaves nothing for the peak; never spent, the story deflates. Great plotting is mostly budget management — which is why a quiet story that compounds small losses can feel enormous.

activities.anchor: the exam skill is E. M. Forster's distinction
activities.caption: file each character by Forster's test
activities.name: hrCharacterBuckets

buckets: flat — built on a single idea, stays fixed

items.label: the miser, unchanged from first page to last
the wise mentor who never wavers
the rival whose every scene runs the same sneer
Elizabeth Bennet revising her entire estimate of Darcy
the timid sister who talks back at the peak — and we believe it

config.why: The deeper rule: character is choice under pressure — watch what a character does when the stakes peak, not what the author's description claims.

activities.anchor: is a point of view with a style
activities.caption: pair each narrating option with what it decides
activities.name: hrVoiceMatch

config.prompt: Who is telling me this? Pair the option with what it does to what can be known:

pairs.right: locks you inside one head — reliable or (the fun part) not
reports a world the reader gradually catches distorting
names whose eyes a third-person narrator borrows moment to moment

config.why: Ask constantly: who is telling me this, what can they not see, and what are they (deliberately) not telling me? The answers account for most of a novel's irony and much of its suspense.

activities.caption: true or false — theme, moral, question
activities.name: hrThemeJudge

statements.s: A moral is an answer; a theme is a question.
statements.why: Which is why fiction's questions stay open — on purpose.

statements.s: The theme is the moral, tacked on at the end.
statements.why: If a story tells you its theme outright, it is an essay wearing a costume.

statements.s: The novels that last pose their question so well that every generation answers it differently.
statements.why: Usually answered ambiguously — that is what keeps the question alive.

statements.s: A story's theme can be settled the way a sum is settled.
statements.why: Theme is the question a story keeps asking — ask instead what each character's fate argues about it.

activities.anchor: spends its whole budget on a single farcical wagon-ride
activities.caption: walk the structural diagnosis, decision by decision
activities.name: hrStructureBranch

config.root: A story's climax feels unearned. You hold the whole text — walk the diagnosis:

choices.label: The climb: did the escalations compound or merely accumulate?
choices.feedback: The right instinct — the peak's authority is built below it.

choices.label: The ending: maybe the denouement can rescue it
choices.feedback: The denouement resolves, soothes or leaves untied — it cannot rescue a peak the climb never built.

ending.text: Back up to the climb: the peak is only as strong as the escalations that led to it — and the preparation was visible from the first page.

climb.text: Compounded — each complication made the original question harder to answer — or merely accumulated, a pile of events with the peak bolted on?

choices.label: They compounded
choices.feedback: Then the peak was earned; re-read the ending for its own work.

choices.label: They merely accumulated
choices.feedback: Diagnosis found: the peak arrived unaided, however big it played.

earned.text: An earned peak. The last structural question: what work does the denouement do — resolve, soothe, or leave deliberately untied?

unearned.text: The peak arrived unearned. Now you can say where the story feels wrong — which is what knowing how to read a story means: pointing at the machine while it runs.

config.why: Structure, not excerpts — how the ending was being prepared from the first page, and how the shape itself carries meaning.

activities.caption: run the four passes in sequence
activities.name: hrCloseOrder

config.prompt: One famous sentence, four tools — order the passes:
items: Voice: the solemn aphorism attached to the most worldly proposition imaginable
Structure: the passive social machinery that quietly names the real agent, the marriage market
Theme: the thesis Austen will spend 400 pages complicating
Function: the inciting device planting the central question in twenty-six words
config.why: Not one sentence of plot summary — every observation is about how the writing works on the reader.

activities.caption: scrub four centuries of the novel rebuilding itself
activities.name: hrNovelTimeline

events.title: Don Quixote
events.text: The earliest works are loose, episodic, picaresque: a protagonist wanders through incidents.

events.title: Robinson Crusoe
events.text: Still the wandering shape — the instrument being built.

events.title: Pamela
events.text: Epistolary form: a story told entirely in letters, exploiting intimacy and the danger that letter-writers lie.

events.title: Pride and Prejudice
events.text: Realism perfected: free indirect style — third-person narration that slides inside Elizabeth's head and borrows her sneering voice.

events.title: When We Were Birds
events.text: Postcolonial and world literature: the arc survives while voice, world and who is allowed to narrate are rebuilt — Creole and lyrical English braided.
